answer: Price identity itself: every new account burns a non-transferable stake that rises with the number of identities already spawned, so an honest operator pays once while a sybil farm pays per node and the cost curve bends into a spiral. The burn acts as a prism, splitting reputation into earned beams and bought ones, so verifiers weight only attested work. An attacker with an ivory-tower budget can buy a few nodes, but the tenth identity costs more than it can ever extract, so the attack dies of arithmetic rather than enforcement.
